evidence.reason: Line 85 only strips the `a/` or `b/` prefix when the value starts with those literals. Git-quoted headers begin with `"`, so a quoted path such as `"b/src/\tprobe.txt"` keeps its quotes and escape sequence; line 92 then passes that encoded value into the path matcher and the allow-list test. Path-scoped denylist rules can therefore fail to match files whose names require Git quoting. This is an implementation defect in existing path-matching behavior, not a new requirement, and decoding before the prefix strip is a routine correctness fix.
